question: Should OpenClaw adopt local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as its initial opt-in, release-tested hosting-profile catalog?
rationale: The proposal creates new named product concepts, configuration selection, and support commitments; source review cannot determine whether those are the desired long-term product boundary.

options.title: Adopt the four-profile catalog
options.body: Approve the stated opt-in catalog, with unprofiled deployments retaining the existing readiness baseline and implementation gated on packaged scenario proof.

options.title: Narrow the initial scope
options.body: Approve only the profiles whose runtime and security owners can support now, leaving the remaining postures as future RFC work.

options.title: Keep readiness unprofiled
options.body: Accept reusable readiness independently but decline an OpenClaw-owned named hosting catalog for now.

recommendation.title: Adopt the four-profile catalog
recommendation.body: Approve the stated opt-in catalog, with unprofiled deployments retaining the existing readiness baseline and implementation gated on packaged scenario proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the evidenced author of both this RFC and the directly dependent readiness proposal, and can route the decision to the relevant runtime owners.
